subject: Post-call: Propose fair-share meeting windows for global pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Kovalenko <anya@datascout.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Propose fair-share meeting windows for global pilot

Hi Anya — great conversation earlier, thanks for the context and for walking us through DataScout's ingestion and compliance constraints. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before scheduling the technical deep dive: 

- Recap: you're evaluating inference infra for an MLP-backed summarization pipeline (batch + low-latency interactive UI). Main concerns: predictable tail latency, cost per 1k tokens at scale, and SOC2 evidence for data retention.
- Next step: technical deep dive + pilot scoping (60–75m). We'll split the agenda between architecture/ops and pilot success metrics. Marissa will own the architecture walkthrough; I'll cover pilot KPIs and billing model.
- Deliverables I attached: mutual action plan (sheet) and a 1‑pager pilot scope. Please confirm if anything's missing.

Because the team spans US / EU / APAC, we want an approach that's fair to all time zones. Rather than a fixed UTC slot that always favors one region, we propose a "fair-share" weekly window pattern where the meeting time shifts week-to-week among three buckets so each region gets one friendly slot over the course of a three-week cycle. This keeps the meeting on the same weekday but rotates the local-friendly hour.

Proposed 3-week pattern (each meeting = 60–75m):
1) Week A (EU-friendly): Tue 14:00–15:15 CEST / 05:00–06:15 PDT / 21:00–22:15 SGT
2) Week B (US-friendly): Tue 08:30–09:45 PDT / 17:30–18:45 CEST / 00:30–01:45 SGT (next day)
3) Week C (APAC-friendly): Tue 22:00–23:15 SGT / 13:00–14:15 CEST / 04:00–05:15 PDT

Notes:
- We can compress to a single 60m meeting if preferred (we'll prioritize architecture first).
- If a strict weekly cadence won't work, we can do biweekly with the same fairness pattern.
- Booking link: https://calendly.com/redwood/pilot-technical-deep-dive — you can pick a sample week and we will schedule the first three occurrences to establish the pattern.

Could you (a) confirm who from your side needs to be at the tech deep dive, and (b) which of the three patterns you prefer (Week A/B/C) for the first meeting? If you'd rather propose concrete slots, send a couple and we'll adapt.

Thanks again — looking forward to the next step.

Warmly,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0119

Attachments: RWI_Mutual_Action_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-scope-onepager.pdf (PDF)

From: Anya Kovalenko <anya@datascout.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-call: Propose fair-share meeting windows for global pilot

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the docs. Quick answers: 

1) Attendees from DataScout: me (lead PM), Michael Tan (infra lead, based in SG), and one security reviewer (may join for part of the call).
2) We like the fair-share idea. For the first meeting, Week A (EU-friendly) works best for us because it keeps the core product and security folks awake.

Question: Michael is in SG and prefers no earlier than 20:00 SGT if possible. Given your Week A time shows 21:00 SGT that's OK — just flagging so we don't push him into a middle-of-night slot for follow-ups.

We tentatively picked Tue May 18 — can you confirm availability? I'll reply with a calendar hold once you confirm.

Best,
Anya
Anya Kovalenko
Product Lead, DataScout
anya@datascout.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Kovalenko <anya@datascout.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 02:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Propose fair-share meeting windows for global pilot

Thanks Anya — happy to confirm logistics and add a proposed agenda.

Marcus: I can host the architecture walkthrough and will prepare the following 45‑minute segment:
- 5m quick context + goals for the pilot
- 20m system architecture: model routing, KV cache strategy, quantization options we recommend for batch vs. interactive, and expected latency profile on our Dedicated fleet
- 10m observability & SLOs: what we measure (p50/p95/p99), how token-level cost maps to routes in the console
- 10m Q&A / next steps (pilot success criteria and data exchange plan)

I recommend we keep the meeting to 60m and follow with a separate 30m billing/contract slot if needed (Ben can lead). For the May 18 date: Marcus, I see an opening at 14:00 CEST / 05:00 PDT / 21:00 SGT — that matches Anya's Week A pick. I'll create a draft calendar invite and include a short deck (architecture.pdf) as pre-read.

If Michael needs a slightly earlier SGT time for follow-ups, we can reserve a standing 30m "late APAC" sync every 3rd week (outside this main cadence) to reduce repeated late-night asks. That keeps heavy technical sessions in the fair window and makes an exception lane for short follow-ups.

On quoting / compliance: Anya, Ben can share the SOC2 artifact pointers during the call; Ben — please pull the artifact links from the compliance folder before the invite.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Kovalenko <anya@datascout.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Propose fair-share meeting windows for global pilot

Perfect — thanks for the quick sync, Anya and Marissa.

I've booked Tue, 18 May 2027 14:00–15:00 CEST (calendar invite sent). Agenda and pre-reads attached in the invite; Marissa will kick off with the architecture walkthrough and we'll keep the last 10–15 minutes for pilot KPIs and next steps. Ben — can you add the SOC2 evidence links to the event and add any billing/contract prerequisites we should prepare?

If anything changes on attendees, please update the event. Otherwise we'll use the Calendly link to seed the first three occurrences so everyone gets a fair rotation of local-friendly times. Looking forward to it.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
